items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-04-07
items.q: No, no, I didn't work with him

ctx.x: How many cymbals did you use?

I used one crash cymbal. Chinese? Chinese crash cymbal. And hit it wide open. Oh man, the drummer was a noisy thing. And the people liked that noise, you know? And another thing too, again, in the days like that, it looked like the lollier play, a lot of people like it. Like that Mr. Clot Miller, buddy, you know? Y'all heard of Blind Gilbert? Oh yeah, I know him. You used to work with him? Eh? No, no, I didn't work with him, but one time we, you see when they draw the crowd, they had my brother and Louis…
Yeah, I was gonna ask you.

items.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15
items.q: You remember a fella too, Blind Gilbert, you ever heard of him?

ctx.x: Bichet was, I'm trying to think, when he was born, he would have been a little bit older than he would have been, Sidney Bichet. Uh, I don't know. See, when were you born? What was the, uh... Me? I was born in 73. You were born in 1890? 1897. 1897, yes. Yeah, born in 1893. And your brother? I forgot what he was born. But was he, he was, was he older than you or younger than me? No, he was younger than me. Oh, he was younger than me. Yeah. He was along with Lewis, you know. Oh, I see. Yeah, Lewis, I don't know.…

You know, the white folks used to have them picking, I don't know, no, I don't think you're old enough to remember Millenburg, Camps. Hey, you're parked! No, I didn't remember Millenburg. Millenburg, West End, they used to have camps. And just about from here to that kitchen, that's just how for a camp, then. And boy, you're talking about, they used to have a Spanish fort, uh, stuff to that kitchen. That is how far the camp's been. And boy, you're talking about, you used to have a Spanish fourth call run out…
a good friend of your brother's. Yeah, that's right. We used to play all the jobs that he couldn't take.
